description: We’re sudo chmod 777 crew, a few SE students who think Mars needs a better map. We’re building an interactive one for the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge and could use more hands. Web dev, design, data viz, writing: if you’re good at any of that, jump in. Bonus points if you’ve touched Leaflet or NASA’s Mars data, but no pressure. Beginners welcome. We’ll figure it out together (probably with a lot of Stack Overflow).
summary: Martian Map is an interactive web tool for planning a safe astronaut walk across Jezero Crater, Mars. Users click a start and end point and instantly get a SAFE, CAUTION or NOT FEASIBLE verdict, with plain-English reasons, based on three checks: terrain steepness, oxygen supply and daylight. It layers five kinds of NASA and USGS data (optical, topographic, thermal, radiation and chemical), including 636 hazard zones, 22 sourced science stops and Perseverance’s real driven path. A Safe Route feature steers around steep ground and favors terrain the rover has already crossed, while live NASA solar-storm alerts and radiation shelter zones address crew safety. Each stop links to its source, and three show mineral data from published research. Planning an astronaut’s walk on Mars means balancing safety against science using data scattered across many sources. Martian Map puts that data in one place and explains its reasoning. We state every assumption and limit openly, including that boulders are not mapped, because trustworthy planning tools must show what they don’t know.
details:
Humans are expected to walk on Mars in the coming decades, and every walk will need a plan. Martian Map is a web tool that helps plan a safe Marswalk across Jezero Crater, where NASA’s Perseverance rover works.

 

What it does: The user clicks a start and end point, or uses Safe Route to find a path between two science stops. The app returns a SAFE, CAUTION or NOT FEASIBLE verdict with plain-English reasons, based on three checks: terrain steepness, oxygen supply and daylight. The map layers a CTX satellite mosaic and shaded relief view, THEMIS thermal data, 636 hazard zones (steep slopes, sand ridges, craters, rough ground), radiation shelter zones with live NASA solar-storm alerts, Perseverance’s real driven path, and 22 science stops with photos and sources.

 

Impact: Mars data is scattered across many sources. We put it in one map that explains its reasoning, so a crew can weigh safety against science.

 

Tools: Python for data processing (elevation, slope and hazard data prepared in advance), JavaScript with React and OpenLayers for the web app, HTML and CSS for the interface, Node.js for local development, deployed on Vercel. It runs in the browser with no backend. AI coding assistants helped us write and debug the code. Every data layer links to its NASA or USGS source.

 

Creativity and factors considered: One verdict built from three checks, always explained. We weighed oxygen limits, daylight, slope, hazards and radiation, and we state our assumptions openly (walking speed, oxygen supply, slope limits). One known limit: no boulder map exists for Jezero, so boulders are not drawn.

 

Scalability: It is built for Jezero Crater now, but the same approach can cover other Mars sites where data exists.
